subject: computing
title: Recursion: factorial(4) — the Call Stack Grows, Then Unwinds

slides.heading: Recursion: factorial(4) — the Call Stack Grows, Then Unwinds
bullets: How one recursive evaluation unfolds: factorial(4) calls factorial(3), which calls factorial(2), which calls factorial(1); each caller pauses on the call stack, the base case returns 1 without calling further, then the stack unwinds as each suspended frame resumes and multiplies to give 24
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we trace one recursive evaluation, factorial(4), frame by frame, and watch the call stack grow on the way down and unwind on the way back up.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Trace the calls in order: factorial(4) calls factorial(3), factorial(3) calls factorial(2), factorial(2) calls factorial(1)
Explain why the base case stops the descent and how the suspended frames resume and multiply on the way back up
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to trace factorial(4) frame by frame and explain why the first call finishes last.

slides.heading: factorial(4) starts first - so why does it finish last?
bullets: factorial(4) is called first, yet it is the last call to produce its value
If factorial(4) is still waiting while factorial(3) runs, where exactly does it wait?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if the first call finished first, what order would the values appear in? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because every caller waits on the stack.

slides.heading: Callers pause on the stack - the base case turns the descent around
bullets: Each call pauses and pushes a new stack frame holding its pending multiplication; the caller waits on the stack, it does not vanish
factorial(1) is the base case: it calls nothing and returns 1 at once
Each frame then resumes in reverse order and multiplies, so the running products are 1, 2, 6, 24
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: a recursive call suspends its caller on the call stack, and only the base case can turn the descent around.

slides.heading: The calls descend: each call pauses and stacks a new frame
bullets: factorial(4) is called first, pauses, and calls factorial(3); that call pauses too and calls factorial(2)
Each caller stays on the call stack, suspended, while the stack grows frame by frame
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the growing stack: factorial(4) has not gone anywhere - it is sitting at the bottom, waiting.

slides.heading: Down to the base case: factorial(1) calls nothing
bullets: factorial(2) pauses and calls factorial(1), the deepest call of the descent
factorial(1) is the base case: it calls nothing, pushes no new frame, and returns 1 at once
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and stop at the base case: this is the only call that answers without asking for help, and it is what stops the descent.

slides.heading: The stack unwinds: each frame resumes and multiplies
bullets: factorial(2) resumes where it stopped and returns 2, then factorial(3) resumes and returns 6
The frames resume in reverse order - last call stacked, first to finish - and the running products build 1, 2, 6, 24
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and follow the values downwards: each frame picks up exactly where it paused and completes its pending multiplication.

slides.heading: The outermost frame returns the answer
bullets: factorial(4), the outermost frame, resumes last and returns 4 x 6 = 24
The stack is now empty: the call that started first finishes last, with the final answer
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and watch the stack empty: the answer 24 only exists because every suspended frame survived to resume.

slides.heading: Worked example: tracing factorial(4)
bullets: First factorial(4) pauses and calls factorial(3); factorial(3) pauses and calls factorial(2); factorial(2) pauses and calls factorial(1)
Then the base case returns 1, and the frames resume in reverse: 2 x 1 = 2, 3 x 2 = 6, 4 x 6 = 24
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, name the call that runs first - factorial(4). Step 2, name the base case - factorial(1). Step 3, state what the base case returns - 1. Step 4, give the unwind products in order: 1, 2, 6, 24.

slides.heading: Your turn: trace factorial(3)
bullets: In pairs: trace factorial(3) frame by frame, naming every frame on the stack and the value each one returns
Then swap and check: did your partner keep every caller alive on the stack until its callee returned?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full trace, then take two pairs answers: descent to factorial(1), base case returns 1, unwind products 1, 2, 6.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who thinks the first call disappears when it makes a recursive call
Name the base case and the order the frames resume in to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers keep every caller on the stack and unwind the frames in reverse order.
